intro_html: This Korean-style shredded pork brings a sweet and savory punch for about $3.92 a bowl (at everyday cost). Lean tenderloin slow cooks in soy, brown sugar, garlic, and ginger until it shreds like a dream, then goes over rice with carrots. It makes 14 servings and hands you 54 grams of protein each.
cost_closing_html: About $3.92 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each bowl gives you 54 grams of protein at 569 calories, with only 8 grams of fat.
upsell_html: Bold flavor, easy prep, and a price that keeps your grocery budget happy. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Fresh ginger freezes well and grates straight from frozen. Buy a knob of ginger and freeze it so it never goes bad on you.
Bagged shredded carrots save you the peeling and cost little. Grab the pre-shredded carrots to keep prep fast.
Tenderloin is pricier, so time your buy. Stock up on tenderloin when it goes on sale and freeze what you do not use today.
make_it: Add the pork tenderloin, sliced onion, garlic, and grated ginger to the slow cooker.
Stir the soy sauce and brown sugar together, then pour it over the pork.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork shreds easily.
Shred the pork right in the pot so it soaks up the sauce.
Cook the rice and warm the shredded carrots for a fresh crunch.
Pile the pork over rice and top with the carrots.
